title: Prediction: Here's What a $5,000 Investment in Nvidia Stock Today Will Be Worth by Year-End 2027
content:
By Adam Spatacco – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›

Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) has experienced abnormal levels of volatility over the last couple of weeks, culminating in the reinstatement of founder Jensen Huang as CEO. However, the company's underlying financial performance tells a much more compelling story.

Nvidia's revenue growth is accelerating, demand for its newest AI infrastructure platforms is expanding, and management recently raised its outlook for fiscal 2028. Even after a dramatic rebound in Nvidia stock, the company's valuation is surprisingly modest relative to its projected growth.

As several product cycles begin to scale simultaneously, Nvidia is poised to deliver another exceptional year of revenue and earnings growth in 2027. I predict Nvidia stock could reach $240 per share by the end of 2027, representing approximately 41% upside from its current trading price.

Nvidia's fiscal 2027 has been remarkable so far. Revenue reached $81.6 billion in the first quarter, increased to $96.2 billion in the second quarter, and climbed to $115.8 billion in the third quarter. That latest figure represented 103% year-over-year growth, while sequential growth accelerated from 18% in the second quarter to 20% in the third.

Most of the momentum comes from Nvidia's data center business, which generated $107.6 billion in revenue during the third quarter, up 110% year over year. However, the composition of that growth is particularly important.

Nvidia breaks down data center revenue into two categories: hyperscale customers and AI clouds, industrial, and enterprise (ACIE). Hyperscale revenue reached $60.1 billion in the third quarter, increasing 71% annually. Meanwhile, ACIE revenue surged 195% to $47.5 billion. This reflects demand from specialized AI cloud providers, enterprises, industrial customers, and other organizations deploying accelerated computing.

This distinction is important because it shows how Nvidia's opportunity extends beyond a handful of major developers. As AI adoption spreads across industries, Nvidia is increasingly supplying the infrastructure supporting a broader ecosystem of customers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26

Nvidia's growth outlook suggests that the company's expansion is only beginning. Management increased its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast from 70% to 75%, citing strong customer demand, improving supply availability, and greater confidence in infrastructure deployment.

To appreciate the magnitude of that forecast, consider Nvidia's current revenue trajectory. The company generated $294 billion in sales during the first three quarters of fiscal 2027 and expects another $130 billion in the fourth quarter. That implies $424 billion in full-year revenue.

Applying management's 75% growth forecast produces $741 billion in fiscal 2028 revenue. This represents an increase of $318 billion in just a single year. That's a jaw-dropping amount of incremental revenue for a company operating at Nvidia's scale. Several catalysts could support this expansion.

First, Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform is scaling alongside existing Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra architectures. Vera Rubin is already Nvidia's fastest product ramp-up to date. Its integrated architecture combines GPUs, Vera CPUs, high bandwidth memory (HBM), networking, and other components designed to improve performance across AI chip clusters.

Second, Nvidia is expanding beyond GPUs into more of the infrastructure connecting them. Its networking technologies, including NVLink, Spectrum-X, and related interconnect products, are important as customers build more sophisticated AI systems. Nvidia's partnership with Marvell Technology also extends NVLink Fusion into custom AI processors and networking equipment, allowing Nvidia to participate in infrastructure spending even while customers choose alternative accelerators to its GPUs.

Third, the proliferation of open models and agentic AI should generate another wave of computing demand. AI agents are becoming capable of performing multi-step tasks that require substantial inference capacity, while open models make advanced AI accessible to more developers and enterprises.

Taken together, these opportunities form the foundation for Nvidia's evolution from a pure-play GPU supplier into a broader AI infrastructure platform spanning hardware and software. Of note, all of these markets are still developing, meaning the next phase of adoption should extend beyond today's hyperscaler capital expenditures (capex).

The most compelling part of Nvidia's investment thesis may be its valuation. Management expects gross margin to hover around 72% and 73% next year. Given those estimates, Wall Street is forecasting Nvidia's fiscal 2028 EPS to land near $16.48. At $170, Nvidia trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of roughly 10.3.

NVDA EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Let's consider what this means for someone investing $5,000 in Nvidia stock today. At an assumed purchase price of $170, that investment would purchase about 29 shares. If Nvidia experiences modest valuation expansion to, say, 12 times earnings, its shares could reach roughly $198 by December 2027. In this scenario, a $5,000 investment would grow to approximately $5,800, representing a 16% return.

However, a slightly more aggressive expansion to 15 times earnings would imply a share price of roughly $247. At this price, the same $5,000 investment would be worth $7,250 -- representing a return of roughly 45%.

My prediction falls near the higher end of the range analyzed above. If Nvidia stock reaches $240 by the end of 2027, that would represent 41% upside from its current price -- turning a $5,000 investment into about $7,000 in just over a year.

title: NVIDIA: Record Earnings, Stock Price Halved
content:
If you had bought (theoretical value/simulation): The reference price will be determined by the opening price of the US market on Tuesday, November 24, 2026 (currently undetermined). Reference value: November 20 closing price of $125.53 (-14.01% from the previous day). The gain or loss on 100,000 yen will be verified in the weekly report.

On November 17, NVIDIA announced its earnings for the August-October 2026 quarter. Revenue was $115.8 billion (+103% year-on-year), a record high.The data center business accounted for $107.6 billion (+110% year-on-year), representing approximately 93% of total revenue. The new "Vera Rubin" platform generated approximately $20 billion in sales in its first quarter of production shipments. The revenue outlook for the next quarter is also strong at $130 billion. The revenue growth outlook for fiscal year 2028 was also raised from +70% to +75%.Yet, the stock price continues to fall. The closing price on November 20 was $125.53, down 14.01% from the previous day. Compared to the closing price of $239.24 on October 6, it is down 47.5%, nearly half the price.There are two anxieties in the background. One is that the California Attorney General sent an investigative subpoena to NVIDIA on November 19, and on November 20, stated that the possibility of criminal violations of state law is also under investigation. It is also reported that the SEC (US Securities and Exchange Commission) is conducting an accounting investigation. The other is that former CEO Huang resigned on November 11, and the company is currently under an interim CEO structure. The closing price on the earnings announcement day (November 17) was $155.46, a slight decline of 0.44% from the previous day, but it fell 19.3% over the three trading days from the 18th to the 20th. More than the strength of the earnings, these two uncertainties are currently being viewed heavily.

Quarterly revenue for data centers went from $35.6 billion in the quarter ending January 2025 to $107.6 billion in the quarter ending October 2026. It has approximately tripled in 8 quarters.The growth has not stopped once. The backlog for cloud orders is $2.5 trillion, an increase from $2 trillion three months ago. Revenue for hyperscale (major cloud providers) was $60.1 billion, up 23% from the previous quarter. It has been accelerating for 6 consecutive quarters.

*Revenue is based on NVIDIA's earnings announcement (8-K to the SEC). Quarterly divisions are based on the company's fiscal year (January year-end).

1. Earnings figures are at a record high, and the outlook is strong

Revenue for the August-October quarter was $115.8 billion (+103% year-on-year), and data center revenue was $107.6 billion (+110% year-on-year), exceeding both the company's own forecast ($108 billion) and market expectations (approximately $109 billion). Vera Rubin generated approximately $20 billion in its first quarter. The outlook for the next quarter is $130 billion, and the revenue growth outlook for fiscal year 2028 was raised to +75%. There are no signs that demand is slowing down.2. Demand is well-supportedThe backlog for cloud orders is $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months ago. Revenue for hyperscale was $60.1 billion (+23% from the previous quarter), marking 6 consecutive quarters of acceleration. Because contracted future revenue is accumulating, current revenue is not a temporary special demand.

The stock price has nearly halved from its October high

The closing price on November 20 was $125.53 (-14.01% from the previous day). It is down 47.5% from the October 6 closing price of $239.24. It fell 22.9% in just the 5 trading days from November 13 to 20, and trading volume on November 20 swelled to 633 million shares. Despite good earnings, the market is pricing in a correction for AI stocks as a whole and concerns specific to the company.

2. The California Attorney General's investigation has expanded to the possibility of criminal chargesCalifornia Attorney General Bonta sent an investigative subpoena to NVIDIA on November 19. In an interview with Bloomberg on November 20, he stated that the possibility of criminal violations of state law is also under investigation. They are investigating whether advanced chips and confidential information were passed to China, and whether the company and former CEO Huang misled investors and the public. Reuters reported that the SEC is also conducting an accounting investigation. The investigation is in the preliminary stage and no conclusions have been reached, but the possibility of profit disgorgement in the event of illegal sales is weighing on the stock price. As a counter-perspective, the state can only handle the part regarding accountability to investors, and export controls themselves are under federal jurisdiction. Nothing has been decided yet regarding whether a violation will be confirmed.3. Revenue for China is expected to be zero in the outlookWhile there was $2.4 billion in revenue for China data centers from licensed Hopper products in the August-October quarter, it is set to zero in the outlook for the next quarter. Due to the direct hit from US-China tensions, one of the growth markets remains closed for the time being.4. The company remains in an interim structure following the CEO's resignationMr. Huang resigned as CEO and director on November 11, and CFO Kress is serving as interim CEO. The board of directors denied Mr. Huang's return and established a new committee for export controls. Mr. Huang's congressional testimony is scheduled for December 1 (closed session). Earnings were released even under the interim structure, but the future of management remains opaque.5. Gross margin is expected to decline in the next quarterThe gross margin for the August-October quarter was 74.8%, but the outlook for the next quarter is 71-72%. The startup costs for Vera Rubin are heavy. The company sees this level as the bottom and expects it to return to 72-73% in fiscal year 2028, but profit margins will decline in the near term.

Plus2, minus 5. However, the weight of the contents is not as skewed as the numbers suggest.Both of the two pluses are structural strengths. There is backing for demand, with revenue up 103% year-on-year and a backlog of $2.5 trillion. On the other hand, the primary minuses are the ongoing investigations (California Attorney General + SEC) and the deterioration in supply and demand, with the stock price down 47.5%. The structural minuses are the zero-China policy and the interim management system, which are also heavy. In other words, it is a composition where "business figures are strong, but legal and management uncertainties are pushing down the stock price."Whether the momentum continues depends on the course of the investigations. If the investigations are resolved in the direction of non-indictment or settlement, and gross margins bottom out in the next earnings report, the conditions for re-evaluating the strength of demand will be in place. Conversely, if the SEC investigation develops into an accounting issue, there is a possibility of further downside. Monitoring points include Huang's congressional testimony on December 1, the progress of the SEC investigation, the gross margin and Vera Rubin progress in the next earnings report (expected in late February), and the Broadcom earnings report on December 9 (the temperature of AI demand).Under SPY rules, only companies with a difference of two or more between pluses and minuses are subject to the monthly simulation. This time, it is excluded because the pluses do not exceed the minuses. However, I will continue to track the results in the weekly report for one month.

Vera Rubin is for data centers and is not a product that individuals buy directly.The benefits are indirect. If the cost of inference drops, it will become the foundation for making AI services like ChatGPT faster and cheaper. The fact that NVIDIA's earnings are strong also means that AI services around the world are continuing to buy that much computing power.However, whether the price of that computing power will drop, as indicated by the gross margin outlook (a decline to 71-72%), will be a period of high costs for some time.

This article is an analysis of technology and industry and is not investment advice. "If I had bought it" is a theoretical simulation. Since the US market opening price on November 24 is not yet determined at the time of writing this article, it will be reflected in the weekly report.

title: Nvidia Stock Is Down Over 30% From Its High. Is It a Buy?
content:
By John Ballard – Nov 23, 2026 at 10:22AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›

Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%), the designer of the graphics chips that power AI data centers, just got its founder back. On Nov. 23, the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after the company announced his resignation.

The stock has whipsawed in November. It closed trading on Nov. 20 at about 48% below its 52-week high on Oct. 6. Following the news of Huang’s reinstatement on Monday, the shares were up over 30% from Friday's close but still about 32% below that October high.

Huang's return settles the biggest question hanging over the stock, while the business never slowed down. Here's why Nvidia still looks like a buy.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26

Huang understands graphics chip technology and the dynamics of the chip industry as well as anyone. He built Nvidia around CUDA, the software platform that lets developers run programs on its chips, which keeps customers locked into Nvidia's hardware. When Nvidia partnered with Intel in 2025, Huang described CUDA as the center of AI's reinvention of computing.

He is also a skilled dealmaker. On Oct. 27, just weeks before his brief exit, Nvidia agreed to invest $3 billion in an equity offering by Meta Platforms, while Meta said it would expand its use of Nvidia's newest Vera Rubin systems and Spectrum-X networking. Deals like that help keep Nvidia at the center of its biggest customers' plans, even as some of those customers develop their own chips.

Huang built Nvidia into the most important technology company to the global economy. It is the dominant leader in graphics processing units (GPUs), which remain the workhorse chips for AI workloads. With its founder back in charge and demand still strong, Nvidia is well-positioned to deliver further upside for shareholders.

Nvidia's results tell a different story than its stock price. Third-quarter revenue jumped 103% from a year ago to $116 billion, driven by a 110% surge in data center sales. Its new Vera Rubin platform, a rack-sized AI computer, brought in nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of shipments, the fastest product ramp in company history. Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $130 billion.

Nvidia also raised its outlook for next year, now calling for revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously. CFO Colette Kress said that Nvidia's supply agreements now extend to the end of the decade.

The biggest risk is customer concentration. In fiscal 2026, one direct customer accounted for 22% of revenue, and another accounted for 14%. If either one pulled back on spending, Nvidia's sales and growth could take a big hit.

Wall Street expects Nvidia to earn $16.61 per share in fiscal 2028, according to Yahoo! Finance. Even after the Nov. 23 jump, the stock is trading at just over 10 times next year's earnings, an incredibly low multiple for a company still growing this fast. Analysts expect earnings growth of about 49% annualized in the coming years.

With Huang back, investors no longer have to wonder who will run Nvidia next, and the company doesn't have to replace a visionary founder.

The remaining watch item is the board's independent investigation, which will proceed to its conclusion. The board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance. If the review turns up new problems, the stock could swing sharply again. Still, the board said it is confident, based on input from senior U.S. government officials, that Huang's return poses no national security risk.

I believe Nvidia stock is worth buying at this price, given its growth and low valuation. What Huang built over the last 30-plus years won’t fade away anytime soon, and he's back to keep building it. Nvidia's momentum is strong, which should benefit the stock in 2027 and beyond.

title: Nvidia Stock Forecast 2027: Can NVDA Hit $300 After Jensen Huang's Return?
content:
NVDA surged more than 30% during Monday's trading session, reversing part of the losses triggered by Huang's November 12 resignation. The extraordinary rebound followed an earlier 28% premarket surge as investors welcomed the leadership reversal.

Nvidia's board confirmed Huang's reinstatement in its November 23 announcement, saying directors had unanimously approved his return.

The decision helped reverse sentiment after NVDA had fallen more than 40% from its previous high during November's AI stock market collapse.

Wall Street is now reassessing Nvidia's valuation.

Wedbush analyst Dan Ives maintained an Outperform rating and a $225 official price target following Huang's return. However, the firm also discussed a potential $300 valuation with Huang leading the company and governance concerns resolved.

That distinction matters: $300 represents an optimistic scenario rather than Wedbush's formal target.

Other analysts remain bullish but cautious. UBS recently maintained a Buy rating with a $220 target, demonstrating that Wall Street expectations still vary substantially.

The strongest argument for Nvidia's long-term valuation remains its financial performance.

According to the company's November 17 earnings release, third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue reached $115.8 billion, increasing 103% year over year.

Data Center revenue climbed 110% to $107.6 billion, while quarterly net income reached $65.3 billion.

Management also projected approximately $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, reinforcing the underlying demand discussed in our Nvidia earnings coverage.

Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform is another potential catalyst. The company has begun shipping Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, with major cloud infrastructure providers preparing deployments.

Continued adoption could support revenue growth throughout 2027, although competition, infrastructure costs and customer spending decisions remain significant variables.

A $300 share price is achievable as a hypothetical bullish case, but it depends on both earnings and valuation.

For that scenario to materialize, Nvidia would likely need continued rapid revenue growth, successful Rubin adoption and fewer concerns about export restrictions or AI investment returns.

The company's broader 2027 stock outlook has already highlighted $250 as a potential recovery milestone.

Reaching $300 would require an additional 20% increase beyond that level.

Governance risks also remain. Nvidia's board has confirmed that its independent investigation and national security oversight work will continue despite Huang's reinstatement.

Meanwhile, last week's AI stock selloff demonstrated how quickly sentiment can deteriorate when investors question infrastructure spending and technology valuations.

title: [Breaking News] Jensen Huang returns as NVIDIA CEO. What happened in the 11 days since his resignation? A summary of stock price trends, concerns, and future outlook
content:
NVIDIA announced on November 23 (US time) that founder Jensen Huang will return as President, CEO, and Director effective immediately. This return comes just 11 days after his resignation on November 12.

The company had just stated at its earnings call on November 17 that it had "no intention of bringing Mr. Huang back as CEO." Six days later, the board of directors has done a 180-degree turn on that policy.

The stock price had just hit a one-year low last Friday, but following the announcement of his return, it has seen a sharp rebound of around 27% in pre-market trading.

This article summarizes the details of the announcement, the timeline from resignation to return, stock price movements, remaining concerns, and what to watch for in the future.

The details announced by NVIDIA are as follows:

Mr. Huang will return as President, CEO, and Director effective immediately

The board of directors, after repeated discussions and interviews with him, was convinced of his integrity and ability to lead the company, and decided on his return unanimously

In making the decision, they received input from senior US government officials and are confident that his return does not pose a national security risk

Colette Kress, who was serving as interim CEO, will return to her role as CFO (Chief Financial Officer)

Harvey Jones will continue to serve as Chairman of the Board

Chairman Jones commented to the effect that "Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and his return is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, partners, and customers."

Mr. Huang himself also commented to the effect that he is "honored to lead one of the world's most important technology companies again at the dawn of a new industrial revolution."

At the same time, mechanisms to strengthen governance were also announced:

A new "National Security and Export Control Committee" composed of independent directors will be established to oversee export regulations and security risks

A Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) will be hired to oversee compliance across the entire company

The independent investigation by the board of directors will continue until a final conclusion is reached. Mr. Huang will also cooperate

This turmoil moved rapidly over the course of just about two weeks.

November 8: Reports surfaced that Mr. Huang had been a target of foreign intelligence activities. The board of directors formed an independent committee and began an investigation involving outside counsel

November 11: A US newspaper reports on new details regarding the relationship between Huang and senior company executives. The board of directors meets that night.

November 12: Huang resigns as President, CEO, and director. CFO Kress becomes interim CEO.

November 15: The Financial Times reports that "Huang discussed his return with close associates." An open letter calling for his return, signed by figures including Elon Musk and the CEO of Epic Games, exceeds 180,000 signatures.

November 17: During an earnings call, the company states, "There is no intention to bring Huang back." On the same day, a US newspaper reports that "the SEC is investigating Nvidia."

November 18: Huang issues a statement on X. He admits to committing a serious personal error and expresses his willingness to return if the board of directors deems it best.

November 20: The stock price plunges 14%, hitting a one-year low.

Morning of November 23: Compounded by President Trump's remark that "Nvidia should bring Huang back," the board of directors makes a sudden reversal and decides on his return.

Furthermore, regarding the woman with whom Huang is alleged to have had a relationship, US authorities suspect she may have been engaged in espionage for China, though the Chinese side denies this.

Nvidia stock fluctuated significantly around the time of the resignation (closing prices, in USD).

Early October: Near all-time highs (52-week high was in the $243 range).

November 4: $200.13 (semiconductor stocks fell following the results of the US midterm elections).

November 11: $173.73 (last closing price before resignation).

November 12: $166.19 (-4.3%). Following the resignation announcement, the stock briefly plunged to $148.80 (over -14%) during trading.

November 17: $155.46 (Day of earnings announcement)

November 18: $150.96 (-2.9%). Despite strong earnings, the stock fell due to anxiety over the absence of top management

November 20: $125.53 (-14.0%). Lowest price in a year

November 23: Sharp rebound to the $160 range (approx. +27%) before the market opened

From $173 before his resignation to $125 on Friday, that is a decline of about 28%. From the October high, it had fallen to nearly half its value.

What is worth noting is that the business performance itself was not bad. The quarterly revenue announced on November 17 was $115.8 billion, about double that of the previous year. The outlook for the next quarter was also about $130 billion, exceeding market expectations. Even so, the stock price continued to fall, so it can be said that this decline was due to anxiety over 'who will lead the company' rather than 'business performance'.

Among Japanese stocks, reactions varied depending on the distance from Nvidia; companies that supply parts to Nvidia saw significant drops the day after the resignation, while manufacturing equipment companies did not move much.

While the stock price has recovered for now with his return, not all problems have been resolved.

The board's independent investigation is ongoing, and no conclusion has been reached. They have stated they will continue to cooperate with government investigations and inquiries. Depending on the results of the investigation, management could be shaken once again.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission) is investigating Nvidia. The focus includes whether the company's disclosures misled investors. This is a separate issue from Mr. Huang's return and has not been resolved either.

Regarding the change in policy just six days after saying he would 'not be reinstated,' governance experts and some institutional investors have voiced doubts about his return while under investigation. It is undeniable that the decision was made under external pressure, including the stock price crash, petitions, and comments from the President. U.S. legal scholars have also pointed out issues regarding whether he can be trusted and how the board will manage the risk of being 'unable to function without this person'.

The board claims they 'received input from the U.S. government,' but it has not been disclosed which government officials provided this input or on what grounds the decision was made. Since Nvidia is a company strongly affected by U.S.-China relations due to export controls and other factors, it will remain susceptible to political developments in the future.

This rise is based on movements in pre-market trading. It is unclear how much of this can be maintained during regular trading hours. Since the stock has moved more than 20% up and down in a short period, it is safer to assume that volatility will continue for a while.

How the US market closes tonight: Will the sharp rebound in pre-market trading hold until the regular market close?

Japanese semiconductor stocks tomorrow: How will Nvidia-related stocks such as Advantest, Tokyo Electron, and Ibiden react?

Board of Directors' investigation results: When and what kind of information will be announced?

The direction of the SEC investigation

Selection of the new committee and CCO: Will the strengthening of governance be more than just a formality?

US holidays: Trading days are limited this week due to the Thanksgiving holiday.

A leader who had steered the company for 33 years since its founding resigned and returned 11 days later. It was an unprecedented development.

It is clear from the stock price movement that the market welcomed Mr. Huang's return. The fact that the stock price continued to fall despite strong earnings likely reflects the deep anxiety over an 'Nvidia without Mr. Huang'.

On the other hand, the investigation into the issues that triggered his resignation is not over, and the SEC investigation remains. It is more accurate to view this return not as 'the problem being solved,' but as 'filling the management vacuum while the investigation continues'.

Rather than feeling relieved by the recovery in the stock price, it seems necessary to continue monitoring the results of the investigation and the details of the governance enhancements.

*This article is intended for organizing information and does not recommend buying or selling any specific stocks. Stock prices are as of the time of writing (night of November 23, Japan time).

Reference: Nvidia announcements (SEC filings), reports from CNBC, Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Decrypt, Forbes JAPAN, PC Watch, Impress Watch, Game*Spark, GIGAZINE, etc.
